cause_fixed: The mlops simulator node names a target set that is not the active target. Packs required by that context are not loaded, because only the selected contexts are loaded. So the missing-pack check, including csolution list packs -m, does not look at packs from that layer, and the build fails when the pack is not installed.
fix_fixed: Workaround: declare the missing pack in the top-level sds.csolution.yml so it is found. Selecting the target set that uses the layer also installs it. The maintainers agreed the issue is low priority, and the thread does not show a scheduled fix.

problems: The fix sentence says the warning goes away once each addressBlock stays inside its own region. The thread never confirms this; the user only thanks the commenter and says they will look for the converter bug that generates the SVD.
cause_fixed: The SVD describes one peripheral with a single addressBlock whose size covers two separate register regions with a gap between them. That range runs into the address space of another peripheral, so svdconv reports an overlap. The SVD format assumes each peripheral occupies one contiguous block.
fix_fixed: Split the peripheral into two peripherals, one per contiguous region, each with its own baseAddress and a small addressBlock (for example, a 0x1000 size for each). Keep the same groupName so both still belong to the same group.

A separate misconfiguration in the example's target-set, which pointed one target at the wrong project-context, also made the report look like a single cause.
fix_fixed: Update to a cbuild build that includes the fix from cbuild PR 684, then rerun the --rebuild --active command. Check that the target-set references the intended project-context.

Cause says the BKPT is run again from the same address on resume; the thread does not state this mechanism.
cause_fixed: A BKPT instruction inserted into program code halts the core on each resume. Stepping leaves the PC at the BKPT address because the debugger did not advance past it, whereas uVision places the PC at the next instruction.
fix_fixed: Newer pyOCD behaves like uVision: step and continue run over the BKPT instruction, so the program proceeds past it.

cause_fixed: When the FLM describes one uniform sector range covering the whole flash region, pyOCD creates no subregions and never copies the FLM valEmpty value to the parent flash region. The region keeps its default erased byte of 0xFF, so the page buffers used for sparse image programming fill gaps with 0xFF instead of the chip's real erased value.
fix_fixed: Set erased_byte_value to the FLM valEmpty value (0x00 for this target) on the affected region and its subregions, using a project-local pyocd_user.py hook as the reporter did. The thread says the issue was fixed by PR #2032, which propagates valEmpty to the parent region's erased_byte_value, but it does not name a release containing that change.
versions_fixed: Reported on pyOCD 0.44.1; 0.45.1 was also inspected, and the related logic appears unchanged there. No release containing the PR is named.

cause_fixed: When a reply is exactly the DAP packet size (512 bytes), the probe ends the bulk IN transfer with a zero-length packet. pyOCD reads one USB packet per command, so it takes that empty packet as the reply to the next command, and the real reply stays queued in the probe. Every later command then times out until the probe is unplugged and plugged back in.
fix_fixed: Make the pyOCD USB receive loop (PyUSBv2.rx_task) skip zero-length reads and keep reading until it gets a non-empty packet, since no CMSIS-DAP reply is ever empty. This change is implemented in pull request #2061, which the thread asks to be checked. Block reads of 254 or 255 words trigger the problem on this probe.
versions_fixed: pyOCD 0.45.1 (Windows 10, Python 3.14) with the Microchip MPLAB PICkit Basic on CMSIS-DAP v2 firmware switched via pycmsisdapswitcher 2.0.2.19. The fix is in PR #2061; the thread does not say it is released.

cause_fixed: The csolution RTE model loads installed packs, not only the packs the open solution uses. When one installed PDSC is malformed, the pack load fails and the error is raised for the whole workspace, even though the solution does not need that pack. The failing path in RteKernel::LoadAndInsertPacks returns immediately when a pack fails to load.
fix_fixed: No fix is given in the thread. A code change that ignores pack load failures for packs the active solution does not require is feasible but has not been made, and a failure must still be distinguished from a missing pack.

The fix's workaround is described as silencing the AP#3 probe error on Series 2 parts; the thread only shows that the setting removes that message on their hardware, which is consistent with the digest.
cause_fixed: The local pack cache used by pyOCD holds no Silicon Labs .pdsc files, so pack find and pack install cannot see Series 2 devices, although the Keil index lists them. Scripted requests to silabs.com return HTTP 403 in the reporter's environment; whether this causes the missing cache entries is unconfirmed. A manually downloaded pack file bypasses the cache entirely.
fix_fixed: Download the Silicon Labs Series 2 .pack file (for example SiliconLabs.GeckoPlatform_EFR32FG22_DFP) from Silicon Labs' CMSIS-pack page in a browser, then pass it directly with pyocd flash --pack <file> -t <device>. To silence the AP#3 probe error on Series 2 parts, set adi.v5.max_invalid_ap_count=0. The thread reports that the workaround works, but no maintainer fix is recorded.
